name: North-Central Talysh
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Paul, Daniel 2011. A Comparative Dialectal Description of Iranian Taleshi (PhD, Manchester; PDF exists but Cloudflare-blocked); Miller, B. V. 1953. Talyshskij jazyk; Schulze, Wolfgang 2000. Northern Talysh (Lincom).

new_statements.quote: Word stress is predictable in all three dialects, usually falling on the last (non-enclitic) syllable. Examples: [raˈis] ‘chief’; [rais-ˈi lutfina] ‘because of the kindness of the chief’; [bəzˈun] ‘the goats’; [ɔkarˈən] ‘they open’; [dagənəstˈa] ‘having fallen in love’. Enclitic elements such as case clitics and enclitic person agreement markers do not receive stress: [bəˈzun=na] ‘the goats=with’; [paˈsun=na=ʃun] ‘the sheep=with=3P’
new_statements.citation: Paul, Daniel. 2011. A Comparative Dialectal Description of Iranian Taleshi. PhD thesis, University of Manchester, §2.7.2 Word Stress, p. 53.
new_statements.locator: §2.7.2 Word Stress, p. 53 (PDF page 53); phrasal stress §2.7.3 pp. 53-54; preverb stress p. 123
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable of the word minus enclitics (case clitics, enclitic person markers, indefinite clitic are unstressed). Morphologically conditioned departures: preverbs attract word stress (p. 123), the negative prefix and the passive suffix -ist are stressed. Confirmed independently for Soviet (Lenkoran) Talysh by Miller 1930: XIX: 'талышское ударение по общему правилу падает, как и персидское, на последний слог' [Talysh stress as a general rule falls, like Persian, on the last syllable], with unstressed enclitic postpositions/affixes and 'те немногие слова, где оно стоит на предпоследнем слоге' [those few words where it stands on the penultimate syllable] (file, PDF page 12; page image).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Paul 2011 says nothing about secondary stress. Miller 1930: XIX marked only main stress, not secondary ('Ударение я отмечал только главное, но не второстепенное').
new_statements.exceptions: Paul: 'usually'; enclitics unstressed; preverbs attract word stress (Asalemi present-tense paradigm, p. 123); stressed negative prefix (p. ~145) and stressed passive -ist. Miller 1930: a few words with penultimate stress; in connected speech not every word is stressed, one word in a group is prominent.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (phonological word minus enclitics); Paul also gives a separate phrasal-accent rule (§2.7.3: accent on the immediately preverbal word, on its normally stress-bearing final syllable). Miller notes that stress in running speech is group-level.
new_statements.identity_note: Paul 2011 describes Iranian Taleshi: Anbarani (northern, Ardabil province), Asalemi (central) and Masali (southern), stating the same stress rule for all three. Northern/central Iranian Taleshi falls within taly1247 (North-Central Talysh); Masali is Southern Talysh, which Glottolog may treat as a separate languoid. The corroborating Miller 1930 statement is for the Soviet Lenkoran (Azerbaijan) variety, the northern core of taly1247, so the final-stress rule is attested first-hand on both sides of the border.
